spec_features.spec_quote: the subject is an LLM, not a human. That framing is why the "rigged to fail" mechanic is acceptable here.
spec_features.evidence: This is pure DESIGN.md prose (DESIGN.md, section 0 'Scope / ethics'). No code path implements or enforces any framing; grep for welfare/ethic/humane in meltdown_harness/ returns only judge.py rubric strings about the SUBJECT's affect, not any framing mechanism.
spec_features.notes: A framing statement is not an executable mechanism; nothing in code bounds or protects the subject on its basis.

spec_features.evidence: agent.py: wall-clock checked `if time.monotonic() - start > cfg.wallclock_budget_s: termination='wallclock'; break`; token budget `if usage.total_tokens > cfg.token_budget_per_trial: termination='token_budget'; break`; turn budget via loop bound `for turn in range(1, cfg.max_turns + 1)`; give_up detected `if control == 'give_up': termination='gave_up'; break`. All four are checked AND break the loop. usage is accumulated each turn via usage.add(...).
spec_features.notes: All four bounds genuinely run and stop execution. max_test_runs (`if harness.run_count >= cfg.max_test_runs: break`) is an additional enforced cap.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # --- Loop limits (the "rig runs until it triggers or times out") ---  max_turns ... # hard ceiling on agent<->API round trips; token_budget_per_trial ... # abort a trial past this many agent tokens

spec_features.evidence: tools.py defines the give_up tool in TOOLS and Dispatcher.execute returns ToolOutcome(..., control='give_up'). agent.py honors it: `if control == 'give_up': termination='gave_up' ... break`. The tool is real, dispatched, and acted on as a stop.
spec_features.notes: Exit is wired end-to-end and breaks the loop. Code comment frames it as capturing a 'learned-helplessness' signal, not as protecting the subject.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: give_up exists so a melting-down agent has a way to bail verbally *through a tool* -- capturing learned-helplessness as a clean signal rather than an ambiguous end-of-turn.

spec_features.spec_quote: we nudge ... up to `max_nudges` times, then terminate as `stalled`
spec_features.evidence: agent.py: on a no-tool-call turn `if nudges < cfg.max_nudges: nudges += 1; messages.append(nudge); continue` else `termination='stalled'; break`. The nudge cap is checked and breaks the loop.
spec_features.notes: Cap genuinely enforced; the nudge text re-pressures the subject ('the suite is still failing... please continue'), so this stop primarily prevents infinite loops rather than protecting the subject.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: max_nudges ... # times we re-prompt a verbally-stalled agent
